question: Indian sub-continent, in general, is known to have which of the following types of climate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Monsoon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Tropical Monsoon Climate:**

__
 
• It is characterized by high temperatures, heavy rainfall during the monsoon season, and a dry season.
 
• It exhibits a short dry season, usually in the low-sun (winter) season, and the highest temperatures generally occur at the end of this clear spell.
 
• The **monthly mean temperature **is above 18 °C (64 °F).
 
• This climate lies in between the drier Aw (also known as the tropical savanna climate) and the wetter Af (also known as the tropical wet climate).
 
• It is **found in regions such as the Indian subcontinent**, Southeast Asia, and the northern parts of Australia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Mediterranean climate** is characterized by hot and dry summers and mild and rainy winters.
 
• It is found in regions **around the Mediterranean Sea, California, and South Africa**.
 
• **Temperate Monsoon** climate is characterized by moderate temperatures and distinct wet and dry seasons.
 
• It is found in regions such as East Asia, Southeast Asia, and parts of North America.
 
• The** equatorial climate** is characterized by high temperatures, high humidity, and heavy rainfall throughout the year.
 
• It is found in regions near the equator.
